title: Can a randomized benchmark's discrepancy distribution be used directly as a residual-bias prior?
question: When emulated external-control comparisons are benchmarked against the randomized trials whose experimental arms they reuse, does a quantitative bias analysis prior built from the raw discrepancies, or from their variance minus both estimates' squared standard errors, give a new submission's bias-adjusted interval its nominal coverage, or must the sampling component be separated with the shared-arm covariance first?
design: Simulated benchmark programs of 15 or 40 comparisons with known systematic bias and mismatch; raw, naive-subtraction, shared-arm and REML predictive priors; exact coverage of a new submission's bias-adjusted interval. 12 cells, 2000 replicates each.
